segments.input: does is_hidden_path do anything different on Windows? the commit says it does more work there

sections.title: answer
sections.intent: A question about behaviour; no files changed.
sections.summary: Windows adds a metadata() call per check; fine for incremental checks, wrong for the main walk.

narration.body: The difference is the metadata() call. is_hidden_entry reads attributes from the DirEntry, which the walker populated when it listed the directory. is_hidden_path gets a bare Path, so on Windows it has to stat. On other platforms both reduce to the leading-dot check.

Yes. On Windows, is_hidden_path calls path.metadata() to read the file attributes and returns true if HIDDEN is set, then falls back to the leading-dot check. That is one stat per call, because a plain Path has no cached metadata — is_hidden_entry avoids it by using what the walker already fetched. On other platforms the two behave identically: only the dot check, no syscall. So is_hidden_path suits incremental checks on a handful of changed paths, and would be the wrong call inside the main walk loop.

sections.title: check GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL before the hardcoded paths
sections.intent: git 2.32+ lets this variable replace both $HOME/.gitconfig and the XDG config; the crate never looked at it.
sections.summary: The match ladder becomes an or_else chain starting at GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, matching git's semantics where it replaces rather than supplements the standard locations.

narration.body: The ordering here is the whole bug. git treats GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL as a replacement for both $HOME/.gitconfig and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, not as another entry in the list — so it has to be tried first, and when it is set but has no core.excludesFile, falling through to $HOME is arguably wrong. I'll match git's observable behavior for the set-and-found case, which is what the bug is about, and leave the empty-value case to the filter.

git 2.32 added GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, which replaces both $HOME/.gitconfig and the XDG config rather than adding to them. So it has to be checked first. I'll rewrite the match ladder as an or_else chain — it reads as a precedence list, which is what this actually is.

segments.input: why check GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL before $HOME/.gitconfig rather than after?
segments.summary: Because git treats GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL as a replacement, not an extra source; checking it after would let a stale ~/.gitconfig win, which is the reported bug. Noted one remaining divergence from git.

sections.title: answer
sections.intent: A question about the fix; no files changed.
sections.summary: Order encodes git's replace-not-add semantics; one edge case still differs.

narration.body: The order encodes git's semantics. When GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is set, git does not read $HOME/.gitconfig or the XDG file at all. Putting it after $HOME would let a leftover ~/.gitconfig with its own excludesFile shadow the one the user pointed at — the NixOS report exactly. There is one place the fix still diverges: when GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is set but has no core.excludesFile, the chain falls through to $HOME, and git would not.

Because git treats GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL as a replacement for both $HOME/.gitconfig and the XDG config, not as another source in the list — when it is set, git never reads the other two. Checking it after $HOME would let a stale ~/.gitconfig win, which is exactly the NixOS report. One divergence remains: if GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is set but has no core.excludesFile, this code falls through to $HOME and git would not. I left it because it only matters when both files exist and disagree; say if you want it matched exactly.

segments.input: the globset path helpers clone the whole path just to strip a prefix. can we avoid that?

commit.subject: globset: reduce owned path copying in globset
commit.author: kmg0308

sections.title: replace clone-and-drain with a tail slice
sections.intent: Stop allocating a full copy of the path just to discard its prefix.
sections.summary: Both owned-path arms cloned the whole buffer and drained the prefix. Copying the tail directly allocates once, at the size actually needed.

narration.body: Both arms do the same thing: clone the whole Vec, then drain off the front. That is two costs — a full-length allocation plus a memmove — when all we want is the tail. `path[last_slash..].to_vec()` allocates once at the tail length and copies once. Same output, strictly less work, and it drops the ByteVec dependency since drain_bytes was the only user.
Both owned arms clone the entire path and then drain the prefix off the front. I'll copy the tail directly instead — one allocation sized to what we keep, no memmove.
